title: Idle-stream checkpointing and per-client quota eviction protocol for partial generations
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Long-running streaming generations that involve tool/function calls and structured outputs are repeatedly causing resource spikes when clients disconnect or time out mid-generation. Current cleanup uses a global TTL and aggressive GC that sometimes drops usable partial outputs needed for client resume and post-hoc inspection. Goals: 1) Introduce a soft checkpointing mechanism that materializes compact resumable state for partially completed generations, including tool-call results and structured output fragments. 2) Enforce per-client soft quotas and adaptive eviction so noisy clients cannot force cluster-wide compaction storms. 3) Provide a compatibility shim so older SDKs that do not support resumable tokens fall back to a conservative retention policy. 4) Ensure deterministic compaction job that converts checkpoints into final artifacts or tombstones, with observability and safety gates for canary rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Soft checkpoints are created within 150ms after a tool-call boundary or structured-output flush for long-running streams
Per-client in-memory quota and persistent checkpoint count enforced; over-quota clients get earliest-checkpoint eviction and a throttled warning sent over the control channel
Resume token format compatible with runtime-1.19; older SDKs receive a compatibility header and a fallback retention TTL of 24 hours
Compaction job runs deterministically and emits metrics: checkpoints_created, checkpoints_evicted, compaction_success, compaction_duration_ms
End-to-end integration tests demonstrating resume after client disconnect for a stream that executed 3 tool calls and returned structured JSON output
No increase in 95th percentile latency for short-lived streams (<2s) in canary region (target <3% relative increase)
tasks: Design checkpoint wire format (include tool-call metadata, KV-cache pointers, last-emitted token index)
Implement in-memory soft-quota tracker keyed by API key + region
Persist compact checkpoint blobs to object store with tombstone + retention metadata
Compatibility shim: add X-Resume-Support header negotiation and fallback TTL path for older SDKs
Compaction worker: merge checkpoints older than threshold or when finalization signal is received
Add metrics and tracing spans for checkpoint lifecycle and eviction decisions
Create canary rollout plan and automated integration tests (create, disconnect, resume, finalize)
Docs: Update SDK changelog and Console docs to explain resume semantics and quota behavior
